plan.contextChunk: This figure sets four triangle sketches in a row, labeled (a) through (d) below, to enumerate the possible outcomes when two sides and a non-included angle are known. All four share one labeling scheme: an acute angle alpha marked by an arc at the left end of a horizontal base, a vertex beta at the right end of that base, an apex gamma above, side b rising from alpha to gamma, and side a hanging from gamma. Panel (a), headed No triangle, a < h, draws a as a short vertical segment from gamma that stops above the base, leaving a visible gap so nothing closes. Panel (b), headed Right triangle, a = h, has a reaching the base exactly at beta, with a small square marking the right angle formed there. Panel (c), headed Two triangles, a > h, a < b, shows a solid vertical altitude labeled h from gamma to the base, plus two dashed segments each labeled a running from gamma to different landing points, one to the left of the altitude's foot and one at beta. Panel (d), headed One triangle, a is greater than or equal to b, shows a broad triangle whose side a slopes from gamma down to beta. Aligning the four under identical labels isolates the one quantity that changes, the length of a measured against the altitude and against b, and shows how many closures each case admits.

interactionPlan.concept: When two sides and a non-included angle (SSA) are given, the number of possible triangles is decided entirely by comparing the swinging side a to the altitude h = b·sin α and to side b: a < h gives none, a = h gives one right triangle, h < a < b gives two, and a ≥ b gives one.

interactions.teaches: With α and b held fixed, dragging a sweeps the construction continuously through no-triangle, right-triangle, two-triangle, and one-triangle outcomes, showing that the count of closures changes exactly at the thresholds a = h and a = b

demo_steps.title: Fixed givens, swinging side
demo_steps.narration: Angle α and side b are fixed; side a is the free side that swings from γ. The altitude h = b·sin α is drawn as the reference threshold against which a will be compared.

demo_steps.title: a < h — no triangle
demo_steps.narration: With a shorter than the altitude, the arc swept by a never reaches the base, leaving a visible gap — no triangle can close.

demo_steps.title: a = h — right triangle
demo_steps.narration: When a exactly equals h, the swinging side just touches the base perpendicular to it at β, producing the single right triangle marked by the square.

demo_steps.title: h < a < b — two triangles (ambiguous case)
demo_steps.narration: For a between h and b, the arc crosses the base at two points, one on each side of the altitude foot, so two distinct triangles satisfy the same SSA data.

demo_steps.title: a ≥ b — one triangle
demo_steps.narration: Once a is at least as long as b, only the far intersection remains on the base ray, collapsing the ambiguous case back to a single triangle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The SSA 'ambiguous case' is not random — the count of valid triangles is fully determined by where the swinging side a falls relative to the altitude h = b·sin α and to side b.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Lay out four equal-width panels in a row, each with its case heading above and its (a)-(d) tag below, all sharing identical labeling: α with an angle arc at the left of a horizontal base, β at the right, γ at the apex, side b on the left slant, side a on the right. Use α = 30° and b = 10 so h = 5, giving clean thresholds. Panel (a) shows a as a short vertical stub from γ that stops above the base (clear gap); (b) shows a meeting the base at β with a right-angle square; (c) shows a solid vertical altitude labeled h plus two dashed 'a' segments to two base points; (d) shows a wide triangle with a sloping to β. Add a separate live construction strip (or overlay on the active panel) where side a rotates from γ as the slider moves, drawing the swept arc and marking intersection dots on the base. Color the altitude h and right-angle marker in a distinct blue, the swinging/dashed side a in red, and highlight the currently active panel with a soft background tint. Cross-fade the altitude guide on toggle rather than snapping.

authoredContext:
Oblique triangles in the category SSA may have four different outcomes. The figure illustrates the solutions with the known sides a and b and known angle α.

Four attempted oblique triangles are in a row, all with standard labels. Side c is the horizontal base. In the first attempted triangle, side a is less than the altitude height. Since side a cannot reach side c, there is no triangle. In the second attempted triangle, side a is equal to the length of the altitude height, so side a forms a right angle with side c. In the third attempted triangle, side a is greater than the altitude height and less than side b, so side a can form either an acute or obtuse angle with side c. In the fourth attempted triangle, side a is greater than or equal to side b, so side a forms an acute angle with side c.

The source contains only the four static panels; the generated figure adds a numeric readout ('h = b·sin α = 5, b = 10') and a live swinging-side mini-diagram that do not appear in the original (acceptable enhancement, but it shifts visual weight away from the primary panels).
evaluation.notes: All four SSA cases (a)-(d) are reproduced with correct marks (hanging 'a' stub, right-angle square, twin dashed cevians + altitude h, single triangle) and correct α/β/γ/a/b/h labels, and the slider/checkbox/step-player/click-popup interactions are functional and pedagogically sound; the main weaknesses are the cramped, undersized primary panels and the fact that the dynamic swinging-side behavior lives in a small secondary strip rather than morphing the four main panels.
action_items: Scale up the four primary panels to use the full viewbox height (e.g. increase XS/YS and BASEY) so they read as the dominant teaching artifact at inline size, matching the source's large clean layout.
Make the 'Side length a' slider also drive one of the four main panels (or a dedicated highlighted panel) so the core ambiguous-case geometry visibly morphs, not just the small bottom strip.
Increase the font size and offset of the h and a labels in panel (c) and in the live strip so they do not crowd the dashed cevians and remain comfortably legible.
